question: During depletion, the oil phase volume fell from 60.19 mL at 29 MPa to 41.35 mL at 20 MPa. By what percentage did it shrink?
rendered:
<document title="Phase Behavior and Mass Transfer During Oil Reservoir Conversion to Underground Gas Storage: Effects on Storage Capacity and Recovery Efficiency">

=== page 3 ===
- As shown in Figure 3, during the four cycles of gas injection, the oil phase interface rises, accompanied by an increase in oil phase volume and a corresponding decrease in gas phase volume. The oil-gas interface increased from 41.35 mL at the

To calculate the percentage shrinkage, first, find the difference in oil phase volume: 60.19 mL - 41.35 mL = 18.84 mL.

Then, divide this difference by the original volume and multiply by 100: (18.84 mL / 60.19 mL) * 100 = 31.3%.
